newsitem.title: CANADA: S Central Saskatchewan floods to peak over weekend.
newsitem.headline: S Central Saskatchewan floods to peak over weekend.

text.p: Southcentral Saskatchewan spring flood levels were forecast to peak over the Easter weekend while floods in the southwest reached their second highest level of the century, a Saskatchewan Water Corporation official said.

"The Poplar River system (Saskatchewan-Montana border) will probably be the second or third highest on record and in the case of the Moose Jaw River it should be the third or fourth highest on record this weekend," Saskatchewan Water Corp.'s director of basin operations Alex Banga said from Moose Jaw.
Southcentral Saskatchewan produces milling wheat and barley. Meanwhile, floodwaters in the southwestern part of the province peaked Wednesday.
"The Wood River basin (southwest Saskatchewan) is very, very close to the flows of 1952 which was the worst of the century," Banga said.
"There's extensive flooding of agricultural land, well into the thousands of acres," Banga added.
Southwest Saskatchewan produced more than 80 percent of the province's durum wheat in 1995/96 (Aug/July) crop year.
The southwest is a major producer of durum wheat and milling wheat, Canadian Wheat Board director of weather and crop surveillance, Paul Bullock said.
Bullock said it is too early to determine the impact of the flooding on upcoming spring seeding.
Canadian grain and oilseed traders said they were watching the flood developments closely.
Record water flows were measured at Lafleche, south of Gravelbourg, in 1952 at 292 cubic meters a second, Banga said.
Since then, Saskatchewan built the Thomson Reservoir to control flood waters. Flows peaked Wednesday morning at the Thomson Reservoir at 226 cubic meters a second.
